messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but they provide sample mean, standard deviation, sample size, and population mean. They likely want the standard error or something? Actually they say "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". That might refer to the standard error of the sampling distribution under H0: sigma/sqrt(n). But we have sample std dev as 1.4; but that's sample standard deviation. For standard error we use sample std dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40)=6.3249. 1.4/6.3249=0.2215 approx.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the test statistic (t-statistic)? Under null, t has df n-1. But standard deviation of t distribution is sqrt(df/(df-2)) if df>2. Here df=39. So sd(t)=sqrt(39/(37))=sqrt(1.05405)=1.0268. But they didn't ask for t's SD. They asked "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" which could be interpreted as standard error of the mean under null. Usually we compute SE = sigma/sqrt(n). Since we don't know population sigma, we approximate using sample std dev. So answer: ~0.2215.

Thus we should calculate using the function? There's a function to calculate p-value. But we can also call it to get p-value. But they only ask for standard deviation. We can compute manually. Provide explanation. Use python? We can just compute manually. Provide result.
